ca_blob_southeast_face_the.blurb: This small face on the Blob sits inside Hidden Valley Campground in Joshua Tree National Park, at roughly 4,200 feet. It has eight routes, mostly trad with one top-rope line. Most of the grades fall in the 5.10 range, with one 5.3 and one 5.7 for climbers wanting something gentler. The climbing is cracks and a flake, plus some delicate lines where protection is sparse. The face gets sun in the morning and shade later in the day, which suits warmer weather. The base is just behind one of the campsites, so the trip from the car is a few steps.
ca_blob_southeast_face_the.approach: Walk the paved campground loop to campsite 21; the routes start directly behind it.

ca_crag_of_doom.blurb: This north-facing dome stands near 8,100 feet at the southwest end of the Glass Mountains, in the Mammoth Lakes area of the Eastern Sierra, in a high desert setting. It has eight sport routes, mostly 5.10 and 5.11, with one 5.7 and one 5.8 below those, and the lines include some multipitch. A darker band through the gray stone is more broken than the rest, the upper pitches are cleaner, and the lower section is still being cleaned, so a helmet makes sense while belaying.

ca_campground_boulders_3.blurb: A cluster of boulders in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite National Park, at about 8,700 feet, within the Tuolumne bouldering zone. It has eight problems and they lean hard: a couple of V2 and V3 warm-ups, then two V6, two V7 and two V8. Most visitors come for the biggest boulder, which has crimps and edges. Bring several pads and a spotter. Trees block part of the sun on the main boulder. The Tuolumne zone as a whole is often cooler than other bouldering areas nearby.

ca_aqualunge.blurb: Aqualunge is a compact wall of eight routes in the Limbo area of Mission Gorge, part of Mission Trails in the San Diego area, at about 600 feet. Six lines are trad and two are sport. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.11, with a cluster at 5.9 and 5.10 and two at 5.11. It branches off the main Limbo trail beyond the big central wall and is easy to spot once you are up there.

ca_atomic_mushroom_boulder.blurb: A single sandstone boulder with a mushroom-shaped profile, in the Castle Rock and Sanborn area of the South Bay, about 2,800 feet up in the San Francisco Bay Area. It has eight problems, from V0 to a V9 direct finish, with several in the V3 to V6 range. The sides give face climbing, and the holds are somewhat smooth and glossy. It sits farther out than the main Castle Rock boulders, past the shooting range, and can be seen from the highway.

ca_corridor_boulders_2.blurb: This set of boulders is part of the Slickrock bouldering area near Three Rivers, at about 670 feet in the Sequoia and Kings Canyon region. It has eight problems on the beach where the river bends. Most are V0 to V3, with a handful harder and the top end near V7. Fall and winter are the usual seasons, since the lake covers many of the boulders from late spring through summer. The spot draws swimmers and tourists, so mornings or later in the year are quieter.

ca_arete_boulders.blurb: A small bouldering spot in the Echo Cove area of Joshua Tree National Park, just southeast of the Echo Cove parking lot, at about 4,200 feet. It has eight problems and nearly all are easy: two are VB, three V0, one V1 and two V2. The boulders are close to the road after a short walk, so this is a handy place to warm up or to start out on low-grade problems.

ca_asian_friends_buttress.blurb: A light-colored buttress in the West Mongolia section of the Wonderland of Rocks, Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,400 feet. It has eight routes, nearly all trad plus one top-rope line, and the grades stay between 5.4 and 5.8, with four at 5.7. That makes it a reasonable pick for newer trad leaders. The walk-in goes past a pointed formation, then along a wash among boulders into a small valley below the buttress.
ca_asian_friends_buttress.approach: Pass the pointed, blocky-topped formation on its right side, then follow a wash through boulders into a small valley beneath the buttress; a wash through that valley leads to the boulder gully at the base.
